content.user_title: Transform Data Arrays With Reusable Operations
content.value_statement: Large record arrays are hard to clean, sort, and summarize inside AI workflows. This skill provides reusable JavaScript operations for common transformations and compact processing summaries.
actual_capabilities: Filters array records with caller-defined conditions.
Maps records to normalized fields and values.
Sorts records by a selected field in ascending or descending order.
Aggregates numeric fields with sum, average, count, minimum, or maximum.
Removes duplicate records based on a selected field.
Returns processing statistics, including input count, output count, and operations applied.
limitations: Requires data to be provided as an array of objects.
Does not include built-in schema validation or type coercion.
Caller-provided filter and map functions must be trusted and reviewed.
Examples reference MCP tools, but the skill does not provide those tools.

use_cases.title: Clean Sales Records
use_cases.description: Filter completed transactions, sort by amount, and summarize revenue before reporting.

use_cases.title: Prepare Customer Lists
use_cases.description: Normalize customer names and emails, remove duplicates, and keep active records for follow-up work.

use_cases.title: Summarize MCP Query Results
use_cases.description: Process database results inside an agent workflow and return compact statistics instead of full datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Start With Filtering
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the data-processor skill to filter this array to completed records, sort by amount descending, and summarize what changed: [paste data].

prompt_templates.title: Normalize and Deduplicate
prompt_templates.prompt: Normalize the name and email fields, remove duplicate emails, keep records age 25 or older, and return cleaned records plus stats: [paste data].

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Numeric Fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Process these orders by summing the total field, then report input count, output count, and aggregate value. Note missing total values: [paste data].

prompt_templates.title: Design an MCP Data Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Query customers with an MCP database tool, process active records with revenue sorting and revenue sum, save the processed list, and return only summary metrics.

output_examples.input: Four sales records with one pending status and three completed statuses.
output_examples.output: Three completed records remain, sorted by amount from highest to lowest. The summary reports one removed record and three output records.

output_examples.input: Customer records with inconsistent casing, extra spaces, and one duplicate email.
output_examples.output: Names are trimmed, emails are lowercase, and the duplicate email is removed. The summary reports the deduplication step.

output_examples.input: Order records with total values of 100, 150, and 200.
output_examples.output: The aggregate result is a total of 450 across three orders.

best_practices: Validate input shape and field names before running transformations.
Return summary statistics when full datasets are too large for the conversation.
Use trusted, reviewable filter and map functions for custom logic.
anti_patterns: Do not pass untrusted JavaScript functions into filter or map operations.
Do not process sensitive records through unapproved MCP storage tools.
Do not rely on aggregate results without checking missing or nonnumeric values.

faq.question: Can it process files directly?
faq.answer: No. It expects an array of objects. Load file content into an array before using the skill.

faq.question: Does it make network requests?
faq.answer: No. The skill shows an informational link and optional MCP examples, but it does not include network request code.

faq.question: Can it merge datasets?
faq.answer: The current implementation shown in SKILL.md does not include a merge operation.

faq.question: What aggregation methods are supported?
faq.answer: It supports sum, average, count, minimum, and maximum.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive data?
faq.answer: Use it only inside approved environments. Review storage and MCP tool choices before processing sensitive records.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is documented for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that can run or adapt JavaScript snippets.
